question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation $y=f(x)$ of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ given that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{tan}⁡2\theta .
$$

The Cartesian equation of the tangent line is $y=$
{{field-1}}$x\,-$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{tan}⁡2\theta .
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /6} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =7\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{4} \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =7{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =7{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{4},\frac{7}{4}).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\frac{7}{4} & =\sqrt{3}(x-\frac{7\sqrt{3}}{4}) \\ y-\frac{7}{4} & =\sqrt{3}x-\frac{21}{4} \\ y & =\sqrt{3}\,x-\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
